pass_a_gloss:
The axe lies at the root of the trees; every tree not producing good fruit is cut down and thrown into fire. God, through the prophet, foretells the future capture of Jerusalem, because Israel, having become hardened and recently having been devoted to idolatrous worship, did not repent. God says, 'What has happened to you that you have all gone up to empty houses? The city is filled with mourners.' Your wounded are not wounded by the sword, nor are your dead dead from war. It seems that this refers to the devastation in the time of Jehoniah. They blame those from Israel, as if they did not even know evil, and thus they are overcome by extremely difficult troubles, knowing what is to come. For they should have been mourning and lamenting, going up to the house of God, promising repentance, and asking for remembrance of their sins and seeking help from Him alone.

Sanctify a fast, proclaim a healing, gather all elders living in the land to the house of your God, and cry out to the Lord intensely, 'Alas, alas, for the day.' They should have done this to appease the one who is able to save, being provoked. They did not even consider doing what was necessary, but rather went up to their useless houses, where there were lamentations and wailing of children, perhaps due to hunger and thirst. This is what happens to cities under siege. The city was filled with the sound of wailing, but they should have cried out to God instead of wailing uselessly. The lamentation should have been for repentance, and the tears should have been shed before God. Before the battle began, before the sword was drawn, before the resistance was planned, the city was already full of dead bodies.
pass_b_english: The axe lies at the root of the trees; every tree not producing good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.
Since Israel has become hardened and recently devoted to idolatrous worship, God, through the prophet, foretells the future capture of Jerusalem.

He says, 'What has happened to you now, that you have all gone up to empty houses? The city is filled with wailing; your wounded are not wounded by the sword, nor are your dead dead from war' (Isaiah 22:2).

It seems that this refers to the devastation in the time of Jehoniah, as they blame those from Israel as if they did not even know evil, and thus they are overcome by extremely difficult troubles, knowing what is to come.
For they should have been mourning and lamenting, going up to the house of God, promising repentance, asking for remembrance of their sins, and seeking help from Him alone.

And he himself taught this, saying through one of the holy prophets: 'Gird yourselves and lament, you priests; wail, you ministers of the altar; enter, sleep in sackcloth, you ministers of God, for the grain offering and the drink offering have ceased from your house; sanctify a fast, proclaim a healing, gather all the elders living in the land to the house of your God, and cry out to the Lord intensely, Alas, alas, for the day' (Joel 1:14).
These are indeed the things they should have been doing to appease the one who is able to save, being provoked.
However, they did not even consider doing what was necessary, but rather they went up to their useless houses, where there were lamentations and wailing of children, perhaps due to hunger and thirst.
This is what inevitably happens to cities under siege.

He says: 'What has happened to you now, that you have all gone up to empty houses?' For why, he asks, in such inescapable terrors, and because of the words concerning your end, and the whole struggle, have you not cried out to God, but have instead fled to empty houses, even though it benefits you nothing?
For this reason, he says they are empty houses.
And why was the city filled with wailing? Not that they cried out to God, but rather they wailed in vain, and they were only being harmed by the evils occurring within the gates.
The lamentation should have been for repentance, and the tears should have been shed before God.
Behold, he says, before the battle began, before the sword was drawn, before the resistance was planned, the city was already full of dead bodies.
